title: Project conventions & architecture (READ FIRST)
description:
Port of git's gitweb (Perl CGI) to Rust. Source of truth for behaviour: ~/IdeaProjects/git/gitweb/gitweb.perl (8491 lines, 30 actions in %actions, ~20 %feature toggles) and static/gitweb.css. ALWAYS read the relevant gitweb sub before implementing.

NON-NEGOTIABLE CONVENTIONS:
- Hexagonal/ECB. Workspace crates: domain (entities+ports+use-cases, framework-free), git adapter (gix), render (templates->HTML), web (axum boundary + config), app (composition root). Dependencies point INWARD only.
- BDD/TDD, Gherkin ALL THE WAY DOWN. EVERY capability produces features at THREE layers: features/domain (pure rules), features/usecase (use-case via ports + gix-built fixtures), features/web (axum end-to-end). All run by cucumber as harness=false test targets. Strict red->green: feature, then step defs, watch them FAIL on assertions, THEN production code.
- gix adapter gets CONFORMANCE specs over gix-built fixtures.
- Test discipline: cyclomatic complexity 1 (no loops/branches in tests), cover zero/one/many (two counts as many).
- Git backend: gix only, behind a Repository port. NO unsafe (unsafe_code=forbid). Fixtures built WITH gix (no git binary at test time).
- HTML MODERNIZED: semantic HTML5, framework-free templates, fresh CSS. Match gitweb behaviour/information, not markup.
- SECURITY: validate + access-control (see safety bead) BEFORE any fs/repo access; no path traversal; respect repo export rules.
- ESCAPING: rely on template-engine auto-escaping for HTML; handle esc_url/esc_path explicitly; guard deliberate raw-HTML sinks (README.html, highlight output).
- ENCODING: to_utf8 + fallback encoding + binary detection live in domain primitives.
- ERRORS: every capability maps domain errors to die_error-style 4xx/5xx via the error bead.
- Explicit type annotations on variables and lambda params.

DONE (not a bead): workspace scaffold + cucumber harness + first domain slice (Age::humanized/class) green vs age_string/age_class.

title: forks: dir-exists-but-zero-forks shows the unlinked '+' span (filesystem -d guard)
description: Carved out of gitweb_in_rust-6i5 (forks view, DONE). gitweb's git_project_list_body folding (filter_forks_from_projects_list) sets each fork-CAPABLE project's 'forks' field to [] BEFORE folding, gated on a filesystem check: it strips the trailing .git from the path and only sets the field if '-d "$projectroot/$path"' (the container directory) actually EXISTS. That yields THREE rendering states for the leading fork column: 1. forks field UNDEFINED (no container dir / non-bare / the bare .git): empty , no '| forks' link. 2. forks field = [] (dir EXISTS but zero forks folded): an UNLINKED + AND the '| forks' link. 3. forks field = [>0]: a LINKED + AND the '| forks' link. OUR DIVERGENCE: the fold runs through the PURE domain rule model::forks::partition_forks, which cannot stat the filesystem, so it has no way to know a container directory exists with zero listed forks. usecase::project_list collapses state 2 into state 1: a project with zero folded forks shows NO '+' and NO '| forks' link, regardless of whether an empty sibling 'repo/' directory exists. This is faithful for EVERY normal case (a project that actually parents forks always has its container dir exist, since the forks live in it) and diverges ONLY for the exotic case of an empty/repo-less 'repo/' directory next to 'repo.git'. EDGE per gitweb_in_rust-sor. The landing list is MODERNIZED HTML verified behaviourally, so exact markup parity is not strictly required, but the tri-state is a real behavioural difference worth a tracker home. WHAT: thread the container-directory existence through a port so usecase::project_list can render state 2 (unlinked '+' span + '| forks' link) for a fork-capable project with zero folded forks. Likely a ProjectStore method (e.g. container_exists(path) -> bool, or a richer fold that consults the store), kept behind the forks feature gate. THREE layers + the empty-sibling-dir edge. See gitweb_in_rust-0et, gitweb_in_rust-sor.
close_reason: Forks empty-container state (gitweb forks => []) shipped end-to-end: ForkState tri-state + fork_container name-guard (domain), container_exists -d port (gix=SafePath+is_dir), usecase state resolution, render fork_cell tri-state + is_forkable forks-link gate, web e2e over real gix store (add_dir empty sibling). Commits 3789098,db4e374,e855f87,01a1f58,b164c2a,a3dc7d2. Gates: fmt+clippy clean, full suite green (1574 scenarios, exit 0), cargo-mutants on 6 changed fns = 17 caught/2 unviable(Default on no-Default enum)/0 missed (is_forkable survivors killed by added domain coverage). NOTE: db4e374 accidentally bundled 9 concurrent-session .claude/skills files via git add -A; not history-rewritten (active concurrent committer).

description:

title: object action: gitlink/submodule base+path resolves to the commit view
description:
Carved out of gitweb_in_rust-2os.6 (object action, DONE). The object action's base+path branch (git_object's ls-tree branch) takes the object TYPE from ls-tree's mode-derived type column, so a gitlink/submodule entry (mode 160000) reports type 'commit' and redirects to a=commit WITHOUT the submodule's commit object existing in this repository.

OUR DIVERGENCE: usecase::object::redirect_by_base_path resolves the path via Repository::path_id (which returns only the entry's ObjectId, not its mode) and then calls Repository::object_kind on that id. For a gitlink the recorded commit id is NOT present in the repo, so object_kind() (cat-file -t) 404s — our code maps that to 'File or directory for given base does not exist', whereas gitweb would redirect to a=commit. So a base+path object request naming a submodule entry 404s instead of redirecting.

EDGE per gitweb_in_rust-sor (submodules / gitlinks, mode 160000). 2os.6 covered base+path -> blob and -> tree (real objects) and explicitly did NOT cover the gitlink case because path_id loses the entry mode.

WHAT: make the object action's base+path branch derive the destination action from the tree ENTRY's mode (gitweb's ls-tree type column) rather than from cat-file on a possibly-absent id, so a gitlink redirects to a=commit (and a regular file/dir still resolve to blob/tree). This needs the path lookup to surface the entry's mode/type alongside its id — either a new/extended Repository port method (e.g. path_entry -> (mode, oid)) or a FileMode::object_kind() applied to the entry mode, mirroring the tree view which already reads entry modes. The tree fixture's 'vendor' gitlink (crates/fixtures add_tree_repo) is ready to drive it. THREE layers where observable + the gitlink edge. See gitweb_in_rust-0et, gitweb_in_rust-sor.
notes: SECOND CONSUMER (from oy5, the no-action default dispatch): usecase::object_dispatch::kind_of_base_path has the IDENTICAL gitlink limitation as the object action's redirect_by_base_path — it resolves the path via Repository::path_id (oid only, no mode) then object_kind, so a mode-160000 gitlink 404s 'File or directory does not exist' instead of serving the commit view (gitweb's dispatch git_get_type("hb:f") reports type 'commit' for a gitlink). When this bead adds the entry-mode-aware path lookup (path_entry -> (mode, oid) or FileMode::object_kind on the entry mode), thread it into BOTH redirect_by_base_path (usecase::object) AND kind_of_base_path (usecase::object_dispatch). The tree fixture's 'vendor' gitlink drives both.
close_reason: DONE. object action base+path now classifies a gitlink by ls-tree's mode-derived type column (FileMode::object_kind, Submodule->Commit) via new Repository::path_entry, so a mode-160000 submodule redirects to a=commit even with its commit object absent (commits a5ef39f port+gix conformance, 4a1a5d1 object usecase). CORRECTION: the bead's second-consumer premise was WRONG — verified by reading git_object/git_get_type + empirical git that the no-action DISPATCH uses cat-file -t (git_get_type), which FAILS on the absent gitlink commit, so gitweb 404s 'File or directory does not exist' there; our dispatch was already faithful, no code change, only a characterization scenario pins the asymmetry (793c990). End-to-end web acceptance over real gix + the 'vendor' gitlink: object->302 a=commit, dispatch->404 (463ad8d). Gates: fmt/clippy clean, full workspace green, cargo-mutants on the 3 changed prod fns = 0 survivors. path_id now delegates to path_entry in both gix and the usecase fake.

title: Capability: commits & diffs
description: gitweb actions: commit, commitdiff, commitdiff_plain, patch, patches, blobdiff, blobdiff_plain, object. Commit view, unified/colourised diffs, plain patch + mailbox-format patches, blob-vs-blob diff, generic object dispatch. MUST handle the diff edge cases: merge / multi-parent combined (--cc) diffs incl. octopus, rename + copy detection with similarity, file-mode changes, binary diffs. Diff presentation is shared across the diff-bearing actions. Drives the Repository diff port. Gherkin-first; parity per gitweb_in_rust-sor. See gitweb_in_rust-0et.

comments.author: elendal
comments.text: Diff PRESENTATION is delegated to gitweb_in_rust-rhf (vendored @pierre/diffs viewer); the unified diff TEXT it renders comes from gitweb_in_rust-5ps. So this bead = the commit/commitdiff/patch/patches/blobdiff/object actions, dispatch, and wiring — NOT a server-side diff colouriser. The plain endpoints (commitdiff_plain/blobdiff_plain/patch) still need byte-exact golden output from 5ps.

comments.author: elendal
comments.text: CONSTRAINT discovered while landing rhf (the @pierre/diffs viewer): the modern diff viewer fetches its diff from diff_url (a param on render's DiffHostPage) and renders it client-side with parsePatchFiles, which wants a BARE unified diff (starts at 'diff --git'). Do NOT point diff_url at commitdiff_plain: gitweb's commitdiff_plain prepends a mailbox header (From/From:/Date:/Subject:/X-Git-*/commit message/'---') before the patch, and that header is REQUIRED output — commitdiff_plain is a byte-exact golden parity endpoint (sor). So this capability must introduce a SEPARATE clean-diff endpoint for the viewer to fetch, served as View::plain_text(repo.patch(from,to,detection).render()) (the 5ps seam, already headerless). Wiring: register a Commitdiff handler returning View::html(document(head, gitweb_render::diff_host::diff_host_body(page))) with page.diff_url = that clean-diff endpoint and page.viewer_module_src = '/static/diff-viewer.js'. commitdiff_plain/patch/patches keep their gitweb-faithful (header-bearing) bodies for golden parity and are the human 'raw'/'patch' affordances, not the viewer source.

title: Capability: commit action (git_commit)
description:
gitweb action: commit (git_commit). The modernized HTML commit page. WHAT it shows (read git_commit, git_difftree_body, git_print_authorship_rows, git_print_log, parse_commit before implementing):

- Resolve hash (defaults to hash_base then HEAD); 404 'Unknown commit object' when it is not a commit.
- The commit/commitdiff/tree page navigation, with parent context in the formats area: '(initial)' for a root commit, '(parent: <short>)' for a single parent, '(merge: <short> <short> ...)' for a merge.
- An object-header table: author + committer authorship rows (name, email, absolute timestamp via the existing Timestamp/timestamp_badge), the commit sha, the tree row linking to the tree view, and one row per parent (commit | diff links).
- The full commit message as a log body (message_body::log_lines).
- The CHANGED-FILES table (git_difftree_body): one row per changed path with its status decoration and per-file links. Ordinary single-parent diff (via Repository::diff) AND combined/merge diff (via Repository::combined_diff, the N-parent table with a per-parent column). This table is shared with commitdiff (2os.2), so build it as a REUSABLE render component.

Status/decoration coverage (gitweb's A/D/M/T/R/C branches): new file (+ mode when special/exec), deleted, modified, type-change, rename and copy (with similarity% and from->to path), mode/perm changes. File kinds: regular, executable, symlink, submodule. Reuse FileMode (short_type/long_type/permission_string/same_type) and ChangeStatus; the mode-change/new/deleted ANNOTATION decision is a pure rule (put the classification in the domain, the markup in render).

OUT OF SCOPE here, carve to their owners: snapshot links in the tree row (->619), ref markers / format_ref_marker (->klg), the 'patch' formats link (patches feature, ->2os.4). blame links in changed-files rows are gated on the blame feature the way the blob view gates them.

THREE Gherkin layers (domain rule(s) + assemble_commit use case over the fake Repository + web e2e) plus parity EDGES per gitweb_in_rust-sor: root/unborn commit, single parent, merge (octopus = >2 parents), rename+copy, mode change, symlink, submodule, missing object (404). Template slice to copy: the tag view (object-header table + authorship row). See gitweb_in_rust-0et.

Domain: new FileChangeNote primitive (git_difftree_body's per-row status note as a pure rule) + FileMode::permission_bits/is_regular; assemble_commit use case -> CommitView with authorship, parents, log body, and an ordinary (diff) or combined (combined_diff) changed-files set, 404 'Unknown commit object' on a non-commit. Strict red->green (mutation-verified); whole workspace green, clippy -D warnings + fmt clean. title: blobdiff: non-commit hash_base degenerate-title fallback (git_blobdiff else branch)
description: gitweb_in_rust-2os.9 shipped the html blobdiff viewer for the COMMON case: hash_base is a commit, so assemble_blobdiff reads parse_commit(hash_base) for the header subject (Repository::find_commit). gitweb's git_blobdiff (gitweb.perl ~7768-7776) has a FALLBACK the port does not: when parse_commit($hash_base) returns nothing (hash_base is NOT a commit — a blob/tree, reachable only via a hand-crafted URI; every changed-files / history / feed link carries a commit base), gitweb still renders the page with a degenerate title 'X vs Y' (esc_html("$hash vs $hash_parent")) and an EMPTY page_path, instead of the commit subject + file path. Our assemble_blobdiff calls repo.find_commit(to) unconditionally, so a non-commit base errors/404s where gitweb shows the degenerate page.\n\nWHAT: bring the non-commit-base branch to gitweb fidelity — when hash_base does not resolve to a commit, the BlobdiffView (or a sibling) carries the 'hash vs hash_parent' title and no file path, rather than failing. Decide whether the resolved hash/hash_parent (the blob ids gitweb interpolates) thread through the view. Behavioural verification (usecase + web), HTML modernized per the slice. Edge per gitweb_in_rust-sor. Low priority: no real gitweb link produces a non-commit blobdiff base. See gitweb_in_rust-0et and the seam usecase::blobdiff::assemble_blobdiff.
close_reason: blobdiff non-commit base degenerate title shipped. assemble_blobdiff now gates the header title on Repository::object_kind(base): a commit base keeps parse_commit's subject; a tree-ish-but-not-commit base (raw tree id in a hand-crafted URI) gets gitweb's else-branch degenerate 'to_id vs from_id' from the resolved FilePatch blob ids. No new port method (reuses object_kind), no error-string sniffing, handler unchanged (pure glue over view.title()). Two Gherkin layers green: usecase (object-kind 'tree' fixture, title pairs new/old ids) + web (tree-base GET via head_tree_and_parent_tree -> 200, ' vs ', no commit subject). title: Capability: patches action (format-patch range, [PATCH i/N] numbering)
description:
Carved out of gitweb_in_rust-2os.4 (the patch single form, DONE). gitweb's git_patches = git_commitdiff(-format => 'patch') — the RANGE form, streamed verbatim from 'git format-patch -M --encoding=utf8 --stdout -<patch_max> -n --root <hash>'.

Reuses ALL the machinery 2os.4 shipped: the FormatPatch entity ALREADY renders a Vec<PatchEntry> joined by 'blocks.join("\n\n") + "\n"' and supports the number=Some((i,n)) -> '[PATCH i/N]' prefix; the Diffstat entity; usecase::patch::build_entry(repo, oid, commit, number) is already pub(crate) and takes the number. So the increment is small and additive.

REMAINING WORK:
- usecase::patches::assemble_patches(repo, revision, patch_max, version): walk history from the revision back up to patch_max commits (Repository::history with path=None, Page limit=patch_max), order oldest-first, number each [PATCH i/N] where N = count, build_entry per commit, FormatPatch::new(entries, version). Same 403 gate (patch_max==0 -> Forbidden 'Patch view not allowed').

- Golden: extend the parity corpus 'texts' branch to a MULTI-COMMIT text-only chain (add a 2nd text commit on top of the existing texts root), capture 'patches' of the tip via the gitweb CGI (a=patches;h=<tip>), commit the golden + reuse goldens/patch/version sidecar. The corpus-extension technique is proven (a non-HEAD branch leaves existing goldens byte-identical).
- THREE Gherkin layers (usecase + web; the domain FormatPatch numbering is already covered by format_patch.feature's [PATCH i/N] scenario). Edges per gitweb_in_rust-sor: single-commit range ([PATCH 1/1]), multi-commit range, pagination to the feature max, root commit.

GUARDRAILS (from 2os.4): (1) the patch/patches branch does NOT emit X-Git-Tag (gitweb pipes format-patch verbatim; rev_name_tag is commitdiff_plain-only). (2) The diffstat width is format-patch's MAIL_DEFAULT_WRAP=72, NOT git show's 80 — already baked into model::diffstat. (3) A merge in the range reduces to first-parent (the combined --cc story is unified separately in 2os.7); document. (4) Binary patch bodies are out of scope (see the binary-format-patch bead) — keep the corpus text-only. See gitweb_in_rust-0et and gitweb_in_rust-sor.

title: Capability: format-patch binary patch body (GIT binary patch, zlib-exact)
description:
Deferred from gitweb_in_rust-2os.4. The patch/patches goldens are captured over TEXT-ONLY commits because git format-patch's BINARY patch body is unreproducible by the gix-only, no-unsafe port.

THE PROBLEM: for a binary file, 'git format-patch' (and 'git diff --binary') emits a 'GIT binary patch' section — base85 of git's OWN zlib deflate output (diff.c emit_binary_diff_body / deflate_it at zlib_compression_level), AND git tries a deflated-DELTA against the pre-image and picks whichever is shorter ('literal <n>' vs 'delta <n>'). Reproducing this byte-exact needs (a) C zlib output identical to git's (miniz_oxide/flate2's pure-Rust deflate is NOT byte-identical to zlib), and (b) git's binary delta encoder. Both conflict with unsafe_code=forbid / gix-only / no-git-at-test-time. By contrast the plain endpoints (commitdiff_plain, blobdiff_plain) emit only the 'Binary files A and B differ' notice (bare diff-tree -p, no base85), which the port ALREADY reproduces.

WHAT THIS BEAD MUST DECIDE/DELIVER (pick one, document it):
(a) Reproduce git's binary patch body byte-exact — requires a zlib-compatible deflate (e.g. binding system zlib, which fights no-unsafe) plus git's delta heuristic. Likely NOT worth it.
(b) Declare format-patch binary-body parity OUT OF SCOPE: emit the 'Binary files ... differ' notice (or git's '--no-binary'-style behaviour) for binary files in a patch/patches mail, and document the divergence from real gitweb. The diffstat 'Bin <old> -> <new> bytes' line IS already reproducible (usecase::patch::binary_change reads object_size) and should be verified with a golden over a binary commit (the diffstat is byte-exact even though the body is not).

ALSO IN SCOPE: a binary-inclusive corpus commit + a golden that pins the parts we CAN match (mailbox header + 'Bin X -> Y bytes' diffstat + signature), with the body divergence documented. The seams: usecase::patch::build_diffstat already handles binary via Repository::object_size; model::patch FileContent::Binary emits the notice. See gitweb_in_rust-2os.4's FOUNDATION WARNING and gitweb_in_rust-sor (binary blobs edge).

title: Capability: real combined --cc merge diff (text primitive + viewer/fallback rendering)
description:
GAP 1, carved out of gitweb_in_rust-2os.7 (which now carries GAP 2 only — the explicit-parent base-aware changed-files table).

WHAT: bring a MERGE commit's DEFAULT commitdiff / commitdiff_plain / patch to true combined (--cc / -c) fidelity. Today every diff-bearing view reduces a merge with no explicit parent to its FIRST parent (a two-tree diff the @pierre/diffs viewer can render), because the Repository port exposes combined diffs only as a STRUCTURED change set (Repository::combined_diff -> CombinedDiff), never as patch TEXT, and the client viewer's parsePatchFiles cannot parse git's combined (@@@ / "diff --combined") hunk format.

1. A combined-patch TEXT primitive on the Repository port (gix adapter): render git diff-tree -c/--cc patch text for a merge against all parents at once — the @@@ -a,b -c,d +e,f @@@ N+1-column hunk format. gix gives the file-level combined set but NOT combined hunks; producing --cc text means porting git's combine-diff line-combining (combine-diff.c / xdl combine): a line is shown when it differs from EVERY parent, with one +/- column per parent. title: Capability: base-aware changed-files table for an explicit-parent commitdiff (GAP 2)
description:
Carved out of gitweb_in_rust-2os.2 (commitdiff html + clean-diff endpoint, DONE); the combined --cc half (GAP 1) was split out to gitweb_in_rust-2os.13. This bead is GAP 2 ALONE — shippable now, no combined-diff text or viewer change needed.

PROBLEM: the commitdiff host page (handlers/commitdiff.rs) reuses usecase::commit::assemble_commit for its changed-files TABLE, and assemble_commit ignores the explicit hash_parent: it always diffs a merge as the COMBINED diff against all parents (and a non-merge against its first parent). But gitweb's git_commitdiff builds @difftree with $hash_parent_param = $hash_parent when one is given (git diff-tree -r $hash_parent $hash — a TWO-TREE diff against that explicit parent), and passes git_difftree_body just ($hash_parent) as @parents, so $use_parents is false and $parent (the per-row blob/blame/history/blobdiff link base) is the EXPLICIT parent, not the commit's first parent.

So when a MERGE is viewed with an explicit non-first parent (gitweb's "from parent N" link: a=commitdiff;h=<merge>;hp=<parentN>), our table wrongly shows the combined diff against all parents, while the nav parentage (FromParent) and the viewer's diff URL already correctly target hp..commit (2os.2). For a single-parent commit hp == first parent so the table is already right; this bug is only reachable for a merge (or any arbitrary hp..h, which the rule below also fixes for free).

WHAT (three layers, gitweb-faithful):
- PURE rule (model::commitdiff, next to diff_base): given (parents, explicit), decide whether the table is Combined (merge, no explicit) or an Ordinary two-tree diff against a single base (the explicit parent; else the first parent; else the empty tree for a root). gitweb's $hash_parent_param / $use_parents choice. Domain feature: zero/one/many parents x explicit/none.
- usecase::commit: generalize assemble_commit to take explicit_parent: Option<&str>, resolve it, drive changed_files through the new rule, and carry the resolved ordinary base in the view (ChangedFiles::Ordinary gains the base oid) so the boundary stops re-deriving parents().first(). Usecase feature over gix-built merge fixtures: explicit non-first parent -> Ordinary against that parent, not Combined.
- web: handlers/commitdiff.rs passes the explicit parent into assemble_commit; handlers/changed_files.rs Ordinary rows use the view's base for their link bases; handlers/commit.rs passes None (unchanged behaviour). Web feature: a merge at hp=<2nd parent> renders the ordinary two-tree table (ordinary rows, blob/blobdiff/history bases at hp), nav "from parent 2", viewer URL h=<merge>;hp=<2nd>.

EDGES per gitweb_in_rust-sor: merge with explicit FIRST parent (still Ordinary, == first-parent diff), merge with explicit non-first parent, root/single-parent unaffected. The -c/--cc combined toggle and combined-rendered table are NOT here — they are gitweb_in_rust-2os.13 (GAP 1).

See gitweb_in_rust-0et and the seams in usecase::commit / model::commitdiff / handlers::{commitdiff,changed_files}.

title: Retrofit otk.3 tag view: tagger row from relative Age onto the absolute Timestamp
description:

Flagged by 4m1's consumer list: otk.3 shipped before the primitive existed, so its tagger date is a known parity slip with no bead of its own.

PARITY FACT: gitweb's git_tag renders the tagger via git_print_authorship_rows(\%tag,'author'), which calls format_timestamp_html — i.e. the ABSOLUTE date (rfc2822 in UTC + a '(HH:MM tz)' local-zone hint, with the 'atnight' highlight when the local hour is before 06:00). This removes the tag use case's only dependence on the injected request clock 'now', so that parameter falls out of the tag use case entirely (gitweb's git_tag never consults the current time). Per the modernization + h2t client-seam rules, the render layer emits the timestamp in a machine-readable, localizable form (e.g. a <time datetime=ISO-8601> element) carrying the human local form, and applies the atnight highlight class via the primitive's is_at_night rule — markup is the render layer's choice; the formatting RULE stays in the domain primitive.

title: render/web: make crates self-covering so mutation scoping is correct
description:
WHY: cargo-mutants scopes the test run to the PACKAGE of the mutated function. When a render function's behavior is pinned only by a web (or parity) e2e suite — not by a render-crate suite — mutating it and running render's package shows it as a SURVIVOR even though a downstream test would catch it. That is a FALSE survivor: it corrupts the mutation report (you cannot tell a real spec gap from a misplaced test) AND it taxes speed, because the workaround is widening --test-package to drag in downstream crates, running far more tests per mutant. We have hit and hand-fixed individual cases already (beads e7u, 12k: is_forkable). This generalizes that fix instead of whack-a-mole.

WHAT: for render (133 fns) and web (282 fns), ensure every function's behavior is pinned by a test IN ITS OWN CRATE. Find the render/web functions currently covered only downstream — a scoped `cargo mutants -p gitweb-render` (and `-p gitweb-web`) with the mutants profile surfaces them as survivors that a workspace-scoped or downstream-package run would kill. For each, add or relocate a covering test into the OWNING crate so that crate is self-covering. Behavior stays identical — relocating a covering test is allowed; weakening or rewriting an assertion is a check-change and is not (check-modification boundary).

DEFINITION OF DONE: `cargo mutants -p gitweb-render` and `-p gitweb-web` (mutants profile) produce no survivors that are merely mislocated coverage — every REMAINING survivor is a genuine spec gap to REPORT, not a test living in the wrong crate. Net effect: correct package-scoped mutation results, and a smaller, accurate per-mutant test set (so the per-mutant test package stops dragging in downstream crates).

CONTEXT: this is the render/web counterpart to the domain capability-split (gitweb_in_rust-6r7) — same underlying rule (a crate must test its own behavior), different crates. domain is already self-covering (96 in-crate feature suites, zero stray #[test]); render/web are the gap.

title: gix adapter: project last-change age (git_get_last_activity)
description:
A project's 'last change' is the age of the most recent commit on any of its branches — gitweb's git_get_last_activity. The projects-list page shows it as a sortable age column and the summary page shows it too, so it is per-project metadata the discovery (gitweb_in_rust-2kf) and repo-overview (gitweb_in_rust-otk) capabilities both consume. Read gitweb's git_get_last_activity (and get_branch_refs for which refs count) before implementing.

WHAT: surface, as part of a project's metadata, the commit timestamp of its most recently updated branch. Carry it on the domain ProjectInfo entity (crates/domain/src/model/project_info.rs), extending the gitweb_in_rust-reh slice that already resolves description/owner/category/cloneurl. The adapter must expose the raw commit TIMESTAMP, not an age relative to 'now': the clock belongs to the view layer, kept out of the adapter so conformance stays deterministic and any golden output never flickers. The existing domain Age entity already turns an elapsed-seconds value into gitweb's age string and CSS bucket, so the view computes (now - timestamp) and reuses it.

PARITY EDGES (gitweb_in_rust-sor): a repo with a single branch; several branches where the most recent commit wins; an empty / unborn repo with no commits (no activity -> the field is absent); only the configured branch refs count (gitweb's get_branch_refs, default refs/heads), not tags.

title: Domain primitive: absolute timestamp formatting (parse_date / format_timestamp_html)
description:
gitweb renders absolute commit/tag/tagger dates through parse_date + format_timestamp_html (called from git_print_authorship / git_print_authorship_rows, git_summary's last-change row, the log / shortlog / history bodies, and the feeds). No capability bead owns this shared rule, so it must be a domain primitive — the absolute-date sibling of the relative Age primitive (gitweb_in_rust-be2) — before its consumers can render dates faithfully. Read gitweb's parse_date and format_timestamp_html before implementing.

WHAT: a pure, framework-free domain primitive that turns a git epoch + timezone offset into the civil date/time gitweb shows, in the format variants gitweb uses: the default human form (gitweb's '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'-style local form in the commit/author timezone); the RFC-2822 form (parse_date's rfc2822, used by git_summary's defined-check and the RSS feed); the ISO-8601 form (the Atom feed and the machine-readable value); plus whatever title/hint gitweb attaches (it shows the date in one representation with the other-zone/age as a title). Do the civil-date arithmetic in-domain (days-from-epoch -> Y/M/D, h:m:s) and honour the no-needless-dependencies rule (no chrono/time crate unless justified). The timezone offset token (e.g. '+0200') comes from the Signature already parsed in-domain.

PARITY / EDGES (gitweb_in_rust-sor): epoch 0; negative tz offset; a non-zero tz offset that shifts the civil date across a day boundary; the missing/timeless date case (gitweb prints nothing — see git_summary's guard on defined $cd{'rfc2822'}); leap-year and month-length correctness (Feb 29, Dec 31 rollover).

CONSUMERS to wire as they land (this primitive is their dependency): the commit and tag authorship rows in gitweb_in_rust-2os; git_summary's last-change row in gitweb_in_rust-otk.5 — NOTE that bead's text mis-states this as the relative 'age from 3y0': git_summary actually renders an ABSOLUTE format_timestamp_html of HEAD's committer date, while 3y0 / git_get_last_activity is the projects-LIST age column, a different thing; the log / shortlog / history dates and the rss / atom feed timestamps in gitweb_in_rust-3bg. Also retrofit the tagger row in the already-shipped gitweb_in_rust-otk.3, which currently reuses the relative Age as a modernization stopgap, onto this absolute timestamp.

CLIENT SEAM (gitweb_in_rust-h2t): the javascript-timezone feature re-displays timestamps in the viewer's local zone client-side, so the render layer should emit the timestamp in a machine-readable, localizable form (e.g. a <time datetime=ISO8601> element / data attribute) that h2t's script can rewrite. The formatting RULE stays in the domain; the render layer only chooses the markup.

LAYER: a pure domain primitive, so it gets the domain Gherkin layer (cover zero / one / many, red->green) like the Age primitive (gitweb_in_rust-be2). Its consumers exercise it at their usecase / render / web layers when they wire it.

title: Tag listing: empty age cell vs 'unknown' for timeless tags
description: Refinement of the tags listing (gitweb_in_rust-otk.2, closed): close the one behaviour gap that slice deliberately collapsed. CONTEXT. gitweb's git_tags_body (gitweb.perl ~6047) renders THREE age states, not two: - a tag with a known creation time -> the relative age (e.g. "3 days ago") - a tag of type tag/commit but with epoch 0 -> the italic string "unknown" - a tag whose ref type is neither tag nor commit (a LIGHTWEIGHT tag of a blob or a tree) -> NO age field at all, rendered as an EMPTY age cell () See git_get_tags_list (~3824): $ref_item{'age'} is only set when $type is 'tag' or 'commit'; git_tags_body prints the age only 'if (defined $tag{'age'})', else an empty cell. The otk.2 slice collapsed the second and third cases into one: usecase::tags exposes age as Option where None always renders "unknown". So a lightweight tag of a blob/tree currently shows "unknown" instead of an empty cell. That is behaviour-parity-adjacent but not exact. WHAT. Make the tags listing distinguish all three states end to end, so that: - a commit/annotated tag with a zero creation time still renders "unknown" (unchanged), - a lightweight tag of a blob or a tree renders an EMPTY age cell (no text, no "unknown"), - a tag with a real time renders its age (unchanged). The domain use case must carry the distinction (it is the only layer that knows the ref's object type and epoch); the render layer must emit an empty cell vs "unknown" vs the age; the web layer proves it through a real lightweight blob (and tree) tag fixture. Modernized markup stands — match the BEHAVIOUR (three distinct renderings), pick whatever clean CSS hook fits the empty case. PARITY EDGES (gitweb_in_rust-sor): annotated tag with epoch 0 -> "unknown"; lightweight commit tag with epoch 0 -> "unknown"; lightweight tag of a blob -> empty age; lightweight tag of a tree -> empty age; ordinary aged tag -> its age. Cover them at the three Gherkin layers, red->green. Fixtures already in place: gitweb-fixtures RepoBuilder::lightweight_tag points a tag ref straight at any object id (a blob or tree id works). No Repository port changes expected — object_kind() already tells reftype apart.

title: name_rev: adversarial mutation golden for the effective_distance +/* boundary (double-merge diamond)
description:
After porting git name-rev --tags as model::name_rev (h9i), a cargo-mutants run
on crates/domain/src/model/name_rev.rs leaves exactly ONE survivor after
strengthening: effective_distance (line 111) 'replace + with *' —
`distance + (generation > 0 ? MERGE_TRAVERSAL_WEIGHT : 0)` mutated to
`distance * (...)`. The two sibling mutants (generation '>' to '<' and '>=') were
killed by the diamond scenario (a commit reachable both as a merge's 2nd parent,
mtag^2, and a longer first-parent path, mtag~3, names as mtag^2 — confirmed vs
real git name-rev over a commit-tree-forced redundant-parent merge).

WHY '*' SURVIVES: for a g==0 (merge) candidate, distance*0 = 0 (vs distance+0 =
distance); for g>0, distance*W (vs distance+W). The orderings only flip when a
commit is reachable BOTH via a g==0 path AND a g>0 path AND the distances cross
the threshold — which for '*' needs a DOUBLE-merge path (d_merge = 2*65535)
competing with a first-parent path of d_fp < 65535: correct '+' names it by the
first-parent form, '*' by the merge form. A single-merge diamond does NOT
distinguish '*' (both pick the merge form). This is a measure-zero topology no
real repo produces.

WHAT: pin the boundary with a domain scenario constructing the double-merge
diamond (synthetic CommitGraph — no gix needed). Get the ground-truth name from
real git via `git commit-tree` forcing the redundant-parent merges, then assert
that exact string. If the topology proves unconstructible-or-absurd at the unit
level, REPORT it as accepted equivalent-to-git by inspection (effective_distance
is a verbatim port of builtin/name-rev.c). NOT a correctness gap.

Same niche-boundary category as the ygu delta survivors (kat) and the
binary_patch tie boundary (u38) — the owner's 'land byte-exact + file follow-up'
pattern. See gitweb_in_rust-h9i (close-reason has the full mutation summary),
gitweb_in_rust-kat, gitweb_in_rust-u38.

title: domain: split the monolith into capability crates
description:
WHY: domain is 820 functions / 15,163 LOC and sits at the BOTTOM of the workspace DAG — all six other crates (app, config, git, parity, render, web) depend on it. domain holds ~820 of the workspace's ~1,400 mutable functions, so a full cargo-mutants run is dominated by domain, and mutating any domain function rebuilds the entire downstream cone. This is the worst DAG shape: the fattest, hottest, most-mutated crate is the shared foundation.

It also violates the project's own screaming-architecture mandate: domain is organized by LAYER (model/port/usecase), not by CAPABILITY. The capabilities exist only as modules (delta, binary_patch, diff, refs, feed, search, tree, snapshot, name_rev, ...), not as crate boundaries.

WHAT: promote the hot, self-contained capabilities out of the domain monolith into their own crates, over a shared domain-core of cross-capability primitives (OID, RefName, the Repository port, shared errors). Each new capability crate MUST be self-covering — its behavior pinned by its own in-crate feature/unit suites. A capability crate whose behavior is only exercised downstream reintroduces the false-survivor problem cargo-mutants has with package-scoped tests (see render/web self-covering bead).

PAYOFF: (1) mutating a capability rebuilds only that crate + its consumers, not the whole 820-fn cone; (2) the per-mutant test package shrinks to that capability's suites; (3) full mutation runs parallelize across crates; (4) the architecture finally matches the stated capability boundaries.

SEQUENCING: walking-skeleton first (see child bead) — promote one or two leaf capabilities, MEASURE the mutation-run delta, then decide whether peeling the tangled core capabilities is worth it. Do NOT big-bang this. Each promotion is its own scoped commit; tests move with the code UNCHANGED (a refactor — identical behavior, suites untouched). Relocating a feature suite into its new crate is allowed under the check-modification boundary; rewriting or weakening it is not.

title: gix adapter: content grep search (git grep at one revision)
description:
Implement gitweb's 'grep' search facet (searchtype=grep, git_search_files): content search at ONE revision via 'git grep -n -z', listing each matching FILE with its line NUMBER and the matching line TEXT. Read git_search_files in gitweb.perl before implementing.

WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE BEAD: split out of gitweb_in_rust-13s. The Repository port's search() returns Vec<Commit> and serves the four commit-listing facets (commit/author/committer/pickaxe). grep is fundamentally a different operation: it does not list commits, it lists file/line hits within a single tree, so it cannot share that return type. 13s removed the dead SearchKind::Grep variant; this bead adds grep's own port shape.

WHAT: a new Repository port operation that, given a revision (tree-ish, gitweb's $hash/$co{'tree'}) and a pattern, yields the content matches. Each match carries the file path, the 1-based line number, and the matched line's text. gitweb caps output at 1000 matches and then shows a 'listing trimmed' notice; binary files are reported as a match with no line text ('Binary file (.+) matches'). The match-highlighting (wrapping the matched substring in <span class=match>) is a VIEW concern and belongs in render, not the adapter — the adapter returns the raw line text and lets the boundary decide highlighting. A new domain entity (e.g. GrepMatch { path, line_no, text } with a binary-file variant) carries the result; it is plain data, so per the ports-vs-entities rule it gets conformance over fixtures, not its own domain feature, unless a pure rule (line splitting / binary detection) emerges.

PARITY EDGES (gitweb_in_rust-sor): zero / one / many matches; matches spread across several files (grouped per file, file order stable); multiple matches in one file (each line listed); a binary file match (reported, no text); a non-UTF8 / fallback-encoded line; case handling consistent with gitweb's git grep default; the 1000-match trim boundary. gix has no built-in 'git grep'; implement by walking the tree's blobs at the revision and scanning lines, mirroring git grep's default (literal, case-sensitive unless gitweb's regexp toggle — which, like the commit searches, is not in the port).

Conformance: Gherkin over gix-built fixtures, red->green. Pure adapter + one domain match entity + one port method.
close_reason:
Content grep (git_search_files / git grep -n -z -F at one revision) via BDD, red->green at two layers.

DOMAIN (pure rule): crates/domain/src/model/grep.rs — GrepMatch{Line{path,line_no,text}|Binary{path}} + GrepResults{matches,trimmed} + GREP_MATCH_LIMIT=1000 + file_matches(path,content,pattern). Per-file rule: empty pattern matches nothing; binary file (NUL via is_binary) reported once iff its bytes contain the literal pattern, no text; text file yields one Line per matching line, 1-based via split_inclusive (git's line model incl. final unterminated line), literal CASE-SENSITIVE substring (git -F, no -i) so a line lists once however many occurrences, matched line decoded via to_utf8/latin1 fallback. 13 domain scenarios in features/domain/grep.feature.

PORT: Repository::grep(revision: tree-ish, pattern) -> GrepResults added to crates/domain/src/port/repository.rs.

ADAPTER: crates/git/src/repository.rs grep() — walks tree_leaves (path order, recursive), greps only Regular/Executable blobs (symlinks & gitlinks skipped, matching real git grep on a tree), delegates per-file to file_matches, applies gitweb's cap (len>LIMIT -> truncate+trimmed, early return). 10 conformance scenarios in crates/git/features/grep/content_grep.feature over a gix-built mixed-mode fixture (text/binary/non-UTF8/symlink/gitlink/executable/subtree) + cap-boundary fixture; new tests/grep.rs harness, [[test]] in Cargo.toml.

Parity vs gitweb_in_rust-sor edges covered: zero/one/many, grouped-per-file-in-tree-order, multi-match-per-file, binary (no text), non-UTF8 fallback, tree-ish accepts commit OR tree id, 1000-match trim boundary. title: Reproduce GIT binary patch body byte-exact in patch/patches (format-patch)
description:
WHAT: For a binary file in a patch / patches (format-patch) mail, emit git's real 'GIT binary patch' body instead of today's --no-binary notice, so the mail is BYTE-FOR-BYTE gitweb's 'git format-patch' output. This removes the documented divergence shipped by gitweb_in_rust-2os.12 (which deliberately emitted the notice because the delta encoder did not exist).

CONSUMERS (scope): ONLY patch and patches (gitweb streams 'git format-patch' verbatim, which implies --binary). NOT commitdiff_plain / blobdiff_plain (bare diff-tree -p, no --binary -> notice, ALREADY byte-exact) and NOT the html clean-diff endpoint (the @pierre/diffs viewer cannot render base85 anyway). So scope is exactly the two format-patch endpoints.

THE BODY (git's emit_binary_diff_body, per file, emitted TWICE — forward pre->post and reverse post->pre): each block is 'literal <inflated_size>' OR 'delta <inflated_size>' — whichever of {deflate(target)} vs {deflate(git_delta(source,target))} is SHORTER — followed by the chosen deflated bytes in git's base85 framing, then a blank line.
- DEFLATE: plain zlib, level 1 (Z_BEST_SPEED), default strategy (PROVEN 2026-06 by reversing git's actual output: the zlib stream header is 78 01; C-zlib reproduces it byte-for-byte). Use zlib-rs (ALREADY vendored via flate2 1.1.9, safe public API — its internal unsafe never touches our forbid(unsafe_code) crates).
- DELTA: gitweb_in_rust-ygu (the diff-delta.c port). This bead is BLOCKED on it.
- BASE85: git's variant uses the RFC-1924 alphabet (0-9 A-Z a-z !#$%&()*+-;<=>?@^_`{|}~), but git's framing is NOT a plain base85 codec: data is chunked into <=52-byte LINES, each line prefixed by a length-marker char (1-26 -> A-Z, 27-52 -> a-z), each line's bytes zero-padded to whole 4-byte groups then encoded big-endian 4-bytes->5-chars. ~25 trivial safe lines, write directly (a base85 crate gives only the alphabet, not the framing).

ALSO REQUIRED (a second, smaller divergence): in --binary mode git writes the binary file's 'index' line with FULL 40/64-hex ids (it implies --full-index for binary), whereas text files stay abbreviated. Today the port abbreviates the binary index too (the --no-binary form). Add the full-index switch for binary files.

UNCHANGED: the 'Bin <old> -> <new> bytes' diffstat row is already byte-exact (object_size) — keep it.

ACCEPTANCE: flip the EXISTING parity golden crates/parity/goldens/patch/binary (already captured from real gitweb; today asserted only on the non-binary frame as a DOCUMENTED divergence) to FULL byte-for-byte equality: our patch == gitweb's patch/binary. Retire the patch/binary_no_binary reference and the divergence-documenting assertions in crates/parity/tests/golden.rs, and remove the divergence notes from usecase::patch + model::patch::FileContent::Binary. Extend the corpus/goldens to cover: a literal-wins case (small/dissimilar blob), a DELTA-wins case (large, mostly-similar blob — the case that actually exercises ygu), a binary create (empty pre-image -> literal-only), and confirm BOTH the forward and reverse blocks. Three Gherkin layers + edges per gitweb_in_rust-sor.

Supersedes the gitweb_in_rust-2os.12 documented divergence. Seams: model::patch::FileContent::Binary, usecase::patch::build_diffstat/binary_change, crates/parity corpus 'binmix' branch + patch/binary golden (ALREADY present). See gitweb_in_rust-sor, gitweb_in_rust-0et.
close_reason:
DONE. The patch / patches (format-patch) binary file body is now byte-for-byte git format-patch --binary, retiring the 2os.12 --no-binary divergence. Five commits: d49435f (domain primitives: model::base85 git base85+framing, diff_delta_bounded git's max_size cap, model::binary_patch emit_binary_diff via flate2 zlib-rs level-1 deflate + literal/delta choice + base85 + two blocks); 768b978 (wiring: FileContent::Binary{source,target} + private BinaryMode {Notice|GitBinaryPatch} + Patch::render_format_patch with FULL index for binary / abbreviated for text; adapter conv::to_file_patch plumbs the blob bytes it already held; usecase::patch uses render_format_patch; plain endpoints unchanged); 9d6a65c (check-change: flip parity golden to byte-exact equality, retire the divergence assertions + binary_no_binary reference + divergence notes); a640dc4 (widen binmix corpus: bigdata.bin delta-wins + newbin.bin create, re-captured, isolated to patch/binary); 6fbb617 (remove dead FilePatch::render surfaced by mutation).

PROVEN byte-exact vs real git/gitweb 2.54.0, all in one parity golden + domain unit specs: literal-wins (zdata.bin literal 7/literal 5), delta-wins (bigdata.bin delta 13/delta 13 -- the diff-delta.c/ygu arm + the max_size cap end-to-end), binary-create (newbin.bin literal 4/literal 0). Each binary file full-index, text abbreviated, forward+reverse blocks both pinned.

VERIFICATION (receipts this session): cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast exit 0; fmt --check / clippy --workspace clean; hex-lint clean; check-guard OK (the check-change commit is the only assertion change, human-pre-approved by this bead); trace-audit Mode B clean; CRAP gate clean for the slice (every new/changed fn under 30; highest changed write_body 19.13; the two over-30 fns create_delta 50.20 + write_extended_headers 34.13 are PRE-EXISTING inherited debt, untouched). cargo mutants -p gitweb-domain --in-diff (TMPDIR off /tmp): 67 mutants, 62 caught, 0 timeouts; the 2 FilePatch::render survivors were dead code, removed in 6fbb617; the 1 remaining survivor (shorter_delta '<' vs '<=', the literal-vs-delta TIE boundary -- provably matches git's strict '<', a measure-zero deflate-size tie no test constructs) is REPORTED and filed as follow-up gitweb_in_rust-u38.

title: Snapshot golden parity: byte-exact archives vs git archive
description:
WHAT. The snapshot capability (gitweb_in_rust-619, DONE) serves well-formed tgz/tbz2/txz/zip archives with gitweb-faithful headers (content-type, inline filename project-version, Last-Modified from commit time) and the correct top-level --prefix directory and entry mtime. It does NOT yet produce byte-identical output to real `git archive`, so there is no golden-conformance lock for snapshot in crates/parity.

KNOWN DIVERGENCES (documented in crates/git/features/archive/archive.feature):
- ENTRY ORDER: gix streams a tree breadth-first (a tree's own files before its subtrees'); `git archive` is depth-first. Byte-exactness requires reordering gix's worktree stream to depth-first, which gix-worktree-stream may not expose — investigate whether an ordering hook exists or the entries must be buffered and re-sorted.
- GZIP HEADER: gitweb pipes through `gzip -n` (no name/mtime in the gzip wrapper); confirm gix-archive's TarGz writer matches (flate2 over zlib-rs) or compress the raw tar with a gzip -n equivalent.
- The tar entry mtime now flows from the commit time (ArchiveOptions.modification_time), and the prefix from snapshot_name — both already threaded through the port, so those are no longer blockers.

ACCEPTANCE. Add a snapshot endpoint to the golden harness (crates/parity) capturing real gitweb's `a=snapshot` bytes over the shared corpus, and prove the Rust endpoint matches byte-for-byte for tgz and zip (the two gix produces natively), or document precisely which bytes cannot match and why (e.g. entry order) and pin everything that CAN. tbz2/txz wrap the same tar so they follow tgz. See gitweb_in_rust-sor for the golden harness patterns.

title: render: 9 body/cell renderers survive package-scoped mutation — verify web-layer coverage before strengthening
description:
## Why this exists

A full mutation run of the render crate (`cargo mutants -p gitweb-render`, 177
mutants) scored **94.9% (166/175 viable killed, 9 missed, 2 unviable)** — strong.
All **9 survivors are one shape**: a `Markup`-returning page-body or table-cell
renderer replaced with `Default::default()` (empty markup) **survives** — i.e.
the render crate's *own* tests don't assert that fragment's output. Zero logic
survivors; every comparison/conditional/arithmetic mutant in render was caught.

The 9 functions:

```
blob.rs:75          blob_body
commit.rs:244       parent_row
heads.rs:65         heads_body
history.rs:89       history_body
log.rs:70           log_body
project_list.rs:101 project_list_body
search.rs:172       author_cell
shortlog.rs:82      shortlog_body
tree.rs:89          tree_body
```

## Triage — READ THIS before strengthening: likely a scoping artifact

`cargo-mutants` ran scoped to `-p gitweb-render`, so it executed **only the
render crate's tests**, NOT the **web-crate cucumber suites** that render full
pages and assert the resulting HTML. These nine fragments are almost certainly
**pinned at the web layer** (the page-level e2e asserts the body that embeds
them), which would make these survivors a **per-package mutation-scoping
artifact, not a real coverage gap** — the known limitation where a unit
exercised only by a downstream crate's tests survives a package-scoped run.

So this is a **report/verify**, not a blind strengthen.

## What to do (decide per function, don't blanket-add assertions)

For each of the 9: check whether a **web-crate cucumber scenario already asserts
the rendered output** of the page/cell it feeds.

- **If yes** → it's a scoping artifact. Either accept and record it (the truth
  metric is a full-workspace run that includes the web tests), or, if you want
  the render crate to be self-covering, add one focused render-level assertion.
- **If no** → genuine gap: assert the rendered fragment (render-level unit
  assertion, or a web scenario that pins that page's body).

**Definition of done:** either a full-workspace mutation run (web tests included)
shows these caught, or each of the 9 is documented as web-layer-covered with the
scenario that pins it. Do not add empty/weak "renders something" assertions to
move the number — that is check-gaming and the mutation pass will expose it.

## Provenance / scope

- Found by the mutation tooling added this session (`scripts/mutation-run.bb`,
  `scripts/mutation-report.bb`). Render score 94.9%; domain (separate, bead
  `gitweb_in_rust-uch`) 86.7%; aggregate 90.6%.
- Sibling to `uch` (domain survivors). Mutation scoped to where it earns its
  keep (domain, render); glue/infra out.
close_reason:
DONE (commit 75063cf). VERIFIED then strengthened. Cross-crate cargo-mutants (--test-package gitweb-render --test-package gitweb-web, the recipe needed to run render mutants against the web crate's tests) settled the bead's 'likely a scoping artifact' hypothesis: RIGHT for 8, WRONG for 1.

FINDING (1 missed / 11 caught cross-crate):
- 8 web-covered package-scoping artifacts (FALSE survivors at -p gitweb-render): the 7 *_body wrappers (blob/heads/history/log/project_list/shortlog/tree) + search author_cell. The web cucumber e2e asserts content produced inside them (e.g. web blob.feature asserts 'hello world', inside blob_body), so emptying them fails a web test — but a -p gitweb-render run never runs web tests.
- 1 GENUINE gap: commit parent_row. Its output (parent id + commit|diff links) duplicates the nav's '(parent: <href>)'; the nav even reuses the same commit href, so no assertion at ANY layer uniquely pinned it. Missed even cross-crate.

DECISION (human-chosen: 'self-cover all 9 now'): made the render crate self-covering rather than documenting+deferring, because excluding files from cargo-mutants is forbidden and the team's fast -p gitweb-render gate (mutation-run.bb) would otherwise report these as survivors forever. 7 new 'render the <page> page' scenarios+When-steps assert each body wrapper's composition (page-header + section title + inner datum + page-footer); search author_cell + commit parent_row got focused assertions on existing scenarios. Mode-B, no production change.

RECEIPT: scoped 'cargo mutants -p gitweb-render' over the 9 functions = 12 caught / 0 missed (was 9 missed). Render suite 218 scenarios green; full workspace suite green; fmt + clippy clean.

FOLLOW-UP filed: gitweb_in_rust-ofv (P4) — document the cross-crate cargo-mutants recipe + its pitfalls in CLAUDE.md/mutation-run.bb (check-infra, needs human approval; the --test-workspace=true form was silently ignored and cost three wasted launches). Memory cargo-mutants-tmpfs-trap updated with the recipe.

title: Cross-cutting: Expires +1d on git_blobdiff (dual-oid hash_base & hash_parent_base)
description:

title: Cross-cutting: Expires +1d freshness header for by-oid content
description:
gitweb stamps an Expires header ($expires = "+1d") on responses whose primary hash is a full object id, because content addressed by oid is immutable and a cache may hold it for a day. Sites (gitweb.perl): git_blob (7580/7749), git_blob_plain, git_commit/git_commitdiff html header (7057/7119), git_commitdiff_plain & git_patch (7994). The common rule is git_get_hash_by_path-style: 'if ($hash =~ m/^$oid_regex$/) { $expires = "+1d"; }' — a symbolic ref (HEAD, a branch name) gets NO Expires; only a literal 40/64-hex oid does.

WHAT: when (and only when) the request's hash is a literal object id, the served response carries a freshness lifetime of one day; a ref-named request carries none. This is HTTP cache freshness (Expires / max-age), distinct from the conditional-GET/304 validator already shipped in gitweb_in_rust-o1e.

This reuses the same View-carries-header + boundary-emits-header plumbing o1e established: the View gains an 'expires' marker the boundary turns into the header. The decision 'is this hash a literal oid?' is a pure domain rule (SafeRef/ObjectId already distinguish oid from refname) and earns a domain feature; the emitted header is verified at the web layer. Gherkin red->green, parity edges: literal oid -> Expires present; symbolic ref/HEAD -> absent; the abbreviated-but-not-full oid case follows gitweb (only the full oid_regex matches).

Depends on o1e (shares the boundary header plumbing). See gitweb_in_rust-0et.

title: prevent_xss blob_plain/README hardening mode
description: Parity gap found in the 2026-06-10 gitweb.perl audit. Upstream gitweb has a $prevent_xss site flag: when set, (1) blob_plain serves content with Content-Disposition: attachment unless the MIME type is on a safe allowlist (text/plain and a few image types — see gitweb.perl git_blob_plain), forcing download instead of inline rendering of attacker-controlled HTML/SVG; (2) inline HTML (README.html on the summary/project pages) is suppressed. This is a security behaviour, not a CGI-ism — without it a repo containing evil.html served inline via blob_plain is a stored-XSS vector on the gitweb origin. We have no equivalent setting. WHAT: add a prevent_xss Settings flag wired into the blob_plain content-type/disposition decision (crates already have content_type::PlainHeaders + View::raw_blob seams) and any inline-HTML insertion points, matching gitweb's safe-MIME allowlist semantics. Spec via .feature scenarios for the safe-type inline case, the unsafe-type attachment case, and the flag-off default.
close_reason: Already shipped — not a gap. The 2026-06-10 audit was wrong that 'we have no equivalent setting'. prevent_xss is wired end to end: Settings::prevent_xss (model/settings.rs), the safe-MIME allowlist + attachment/inline disposition in model/content_type.rs (is_inline_safe = text/<lc-alpha> | image/{gif,png,jpeg}, matching gitweb m!^(?:text/[a-z]+|image/(?:gif|png|jpeg))(?:[ ;]|$)!), README.html suppression in usecase/summary.rs (if settings.prevent_xss()), config loader read (config/loader.rs), and the web blob_plain/summary handlers pass it through. All three requested scenarios exist and are GREEN: domain content_type.feature ('XSS prevention forces an attachment for octet-stream', 'still serves text/plain inline', 'still serves a known image inline') + the flag-off defaults. gitweb's text/html->text/plain coercion and svg-attachment paths are only reachable via the optional $mimetypes_file//etc/mime.types lookup, which model/content_type.rs deliberately omits (documented) and which is a separate concern from prevent_xss. title: Repository::rev_name_tag: full name-rev ancestor-distance naming (X-Git-Tag ~N suffix)
description:
gitweb_in_rust-2os.8 shipped rev_name_tag as git name-rev --tags DISTANCE-ZERO ONLY: a tag whose tip is exactly the commit (lightweight -> <name>, annotated -> <name>^0). Real git name-rev --tags also names a commit that sits SOME GENERATIONS BEHIND a tag, suffixing the generation distance (e.g. a commit three before v1.0 -> "v1.0~3", and "v1.0^0~3"-style for the dereference+ancestor mix). gitweb stamps that whole string on the commitdiff_plain / patch X-Git-Tag line. Our subset returns None for such an ancestor-only-named commit, OMITTING the X-Git-Tag line where gitweb emits "X-Git-Tag: v1.0~3" -- a real parity divergence, currently documented in crates/domain/src/port/repository.rs (rev_name_tag doc) and the gix impl in crates/git/src/repository.rs.

WHAT: extend the gix rev_name_tag to replicate git name-rev --tags ancestor-distance naming -- a reverse-reachability walk from each tag ref toward the target commit, picking the closest tag and emitting its name with the right ~N (and ^0 dereference) suffix, matching name-rev byte for byte. Also replicate name-rev's MULTI-TAG tie-break (when several tags can name the commit, which one wins -- our subset takes the first in ref-name order). Read git name-rev (builtin/name-rev.c) before implementing; verify exact output empirically for: tag exactly at commit (regression: lightweight/annotated already pass), commit N behind a single tag, commit reachable from two tags at different distances, annotated-tag dereference combined with ancestor distance.

VERIFY: adapter conformance (Gherkin, crates/git/tests/conformance.rs already has the distance-zero cases under "rev_name_tag" -- add the ancestor cases to crates/git/features/conformance/object_reads.feature), plus a golden over a corpus commit named only by ancestor distance (extend crates/parity/src/corpus.rs + capture-goldens.sh; mind golden ripple -- a new commit on HEAD shifts other goldens, so add it off a side branch like build_diffs_branch did, or accept and recapture). Low priority parity nicety; release commits (the common case) ARE tagged exactly and already covered. See gitweb_in_rust-0et, gitweb_in_rust-sor.
close_reason: DONE — full byte-exact name-rev --tags ancestor naming, retiring the distance-zero subset. gitweb now stamps X-Git-Tag: <tag>~N (and ^N merge form) for a commit some generations behind a tag, where the old impl emitted nothing (a real parity divergence). Four commits: (1) e392f04 domain entity model::name_rev — verbatim port of git name_rev/is_better_name/get_parent_name/get_rev_name, 10 scenarios all confirmed vs real git name-rev (^0 stripped before ~N, ^N merge with gen reset, nearer-eff wins, older-tag tie-break, the surprising merge-penalty mtag^2-beats-mtag~3); cutoff omitted (provably output-identical for one target). ObjectId gained Hash. (2) 48848a3 gix adapter delegates: resolve_tag_tip (peel + tagger/committer date + deref) -> collect_ancestry -> name_by_tags; conformance on an isolated tagged-history fixture (ancestor ~N, tie-break, tree-tag=None), distance-zero stays in object_reads. (3) 510c4de parity golden X-Git-Tag: v2.0~1 byte-exact vs REAL gitweb.perl (new disjoint anchored corpus branch, zero ripple). (4) 4653ce6 hardening: diamond scenario + CRAP refactor (peel_one_tag/commit_at) bringing all changed fns under 30. Verification: workspace cargo test exit 0 (1672 scenarios); fmt/clippy/hex-lint/check-guard/trace-audit clean; cargo mutants -p gitweb-domain -f name_rev.rs = 38 caught, 2 unviable, 1 reported survivor (effective_distance +/* double-merge boundary, filed 6im); CRAP clean for the slice (no changed fn over 30). Follow-up: 6im.

title: gix adapter: snapshot archive bytes (tgz/tbz2/txz/zip)
description:
Implement the Repository ports archive operation in the gix adapter: the bytes of a snapshot archive of a tree in each enabled format (tgz, tbz2, txz, zip, per the ArchiveFormat variants). Read the relevant gitweb snapshot code first and match its behaviour.

Parity edges the Gherkin must cover (gitweb_in_rust-sor): each format; an empty tree; a tree containing executables, symlinks, and submodules represented correctly in the archive; deterministic, reproducible bytes so the same tree always yields the same archive.

Conformance: Gherkin over gix-built fixtures, red->green. Snapshot output is format-stable, so byte-exact bytes are additionally covered by golden differential conformance per gitweb_in_rust-sor when that endpoint lands. Pure adapter. Builds on gitweb_in_rust-a10; unblocks snapshot.
close_reason: Implemented Repository::archive in the gix adapter, BDD red->green over gix-built fixtures: 18 scenarios across all four formats (tgz/tbz2/txz/zip) green. New module crates/git/src/archive.rs drives gix worktree_stream -> worktree_archive (Tar/TarGz/Zip native, pure-Rust flate2/zlib-rs + rawzip) and compresses the raw Tar for tbz2/txz with pure-Rust backends (bzip2 libbz2-rs-sys, lzma-rust2 with unsafe 'optimization' OFF) -- no C FFI, no unsafe in our crates, consistent with the zlib-rs precedent. modification_time pinned to a constant so every format is byte-reproducible (the bead's core parity edge). Entry representation matches git archive's default: regular 0644 / exec 0755 / symlink-as-symlink / subtree recursed / gitlink(submodule) skipped; empty tree -> well-formed file-less archive; non-tree-ish rejected as Invalid via require_tree (gitweb 400). Parity DEFERRED to the snapshot endpoint per the bead: download filename + --prefix (snapshot_name) and byte-exact-vs-git-archive golden bytes -- gix streams BFS (tree's files before subtrees') vs git's DFS, deterministic but a different order. gix gotcha: worktree-archive is not a default feature AND gix does not forward gix-archive's container features, so a direct gix-archive dep with tar/tar_gz/zip is required (recorded in memory). cargo test (whole workspace) + clippy -D warnings + fmt all green.

title: delta: adversarial mutation goldens for niche encoder paths (4096 cutoff, tie-break, short-source clamp, cull pruning)
description:
After porting git's diff-delta.c (gitweb_in_rust-ygu), a full cargo-mutants run on crates/domain/src/model/delta.rs leaves 30 survivors against the 11-scenario golden corpus. 26 are deliberately NOT pinned and are reported as accepted in ygu's close-reason: 6 are PROVABLY EQUIVALENT (e.g. (val<<8)|b == (val<<8)^b because val<<8 has a zero low byte -- lines 117/290/301/359; and 'if x>y{x=y}' == 'if x>=y{x=y}' at line 211; and a dead msize<=4096 recompute guard at 356), 6 need GB/16MB-scale fixtures absurd for a unit suite (4GB-source hash guard line 93, 4GB-offset overflow line 352, >=16MB-offset byte lines 258/259), and 14 are git's index-sizing + bucket-culling PERFORMANCE heuristics that are empirically output-invariant -- the cull_buckets->noop mutant (line 160) survives even the 65541-byte golden, proving culling changes no output byte for it (lines 93-on for sizing, 122/134 coalesce+count, 160/168/169/174 cull).

WHAT this bead pins: the 4 remaining survivors are real-but-niche encoder behaviors the current corpus does not reach. Pin each with a golden captured from REAL git via 'test-tool delta' (extend crates/domain/tests/delta_goldens_capture.sh and crates/domain/features/domain/delta.feature IN LOCKSTEP -- the script header demands it; never fabricate the expected bytes):
- find_longest_match:229 'if msize >= 4096 break' (greedy 'good enough' cutoff): a target position where ONE bucket holds two matching-val source blocks, the first >=4096 bytes and a later one strictly longer, so the cutoff changes which (offset,size) copy is emitted.
- find_longest_match:226 'if msize < matched' (tie-break): two EQUAL-length matches at distinct source offsets in one bucket; encoder keeps the lower offset (buckets are lowest-offset-first), the <= mutant would take the higher.

title: gix adapter: copy detection (-C / gitweb @diff_opts)
description:
Rename+copy detection for the two-tree diff, matching gitweb configured with copy detection. gitweb's default is @diff_opts = ('-M') (renames only); '-C' (copies, implies -M) and '-C --find-copies-harder' are opt-in via configuration. Split out of gitweb_in_rust-fmz, which delivered renames-only at git's default 50% similarity.

WHY DEFERRED: investigation during fmz showed gix 0.84's tree-diff copy tracking does NOT surface copies for the obvious fixtures — with rewrites.copies = Some(Copies { source: FromSetOfModifiedFiles | FromSetOfModifiedFilesAndAllSources, .. }), an exact copy was still reported as a plain Addition, not Change::Rewrite { copy: true }. This bead must first establish (via a probe/fixtures) the exact conditions under which gix emits a copy, or conclude that copy detection must be computed on top of gix's changes, before wiring it behind the Repository port.

ALSO: similarity for INEXACT copies/renames. fmz reports 100 for an exact rewrite (gix sets diff: None when source_id == id) and falls back to gix's DiffLineStats.similarity otherwise; that ratio is NOT git's similarity index. If copy/rename similarity must be byte-exact (e.g. the 'similarity index NN%' line in patch output), that exactness belongs here or in the patch endpoint, not in the raw difftree adapter.

Parity edges (gitweb_in_rust-sor): exact copy; near-copy above/below threshold; copy of an unchanged source vs a modified source; copy + rename in one diff. Map Change::Rewrite { copy: true } -> ChangeStatus::Copied (a domain ChangeStatus::copied(similarity) constructor is needed; ChangeStatus already has the Copied kind and parses 'C<score>').

Conformance: Gherkin over gix-built fixtures, red->green. Pure adapter (+ small domain constructor). Builds on gitweb_in_rust-fmz.
close_reason: Copy detection wired behind the Repository port. Probe established gix 0.84's exact copy behaviour (recorded in gix-adapter-gotchas memory): gix DOES emit Rewrite{copy:true}, source selection matches git (-C = modified set, --find-copies-harder = all sources), but with 3 divergences — it shadows a modified copy-source's own M, computes similarity against the post-image, and skips a lone-copy commit (has_work gate). Added domain port value RenameDetection {RenamesOnly(-M)/Copies(-C)/CopiesHarder(--find-copies-harder)} threaded through diff()/patch(). Adapter uses a TWO-PASS MERGE: renames-only base (faithful M/A/D/R, no shadowing) + a copies pass that only yields copy pairs, then reclassifies the matching addition to Copied with the from-side = source PRE-image (from tree), exact pre-image == to-side -> 100, else gix's similarity hint. Conformance: 9 new copy scenarios in features/diff (renames-only ignores copies; -C finds modified-source copy + ignores unchanged source + keeps source's own M; harder finds exact unchanged-source copy + near-copy above threshold, rejects below; rename+copy together), red->green. title: gix adapter: filesystem owner fallback for project owner
description:
gitweb resolves a project's owner in priority order (git_get_project_owner): the projects-list-file owner, then the gitweb.owner config value, then — as a last resort — the operating-system owner of the repository directory (get_file_owner: the passwd display name of the directory's uid). WHAT (not how): add a short subsection to the project's mutation docs describing the verified recipe and its pitfalls, so the next person does not burn three launches rediscovering it (as happened in e7u).

Verified facts to capture:
- Recipe: 'cargo mutants -f <files> --re <fns> --test-package <mutated-crate> --test-package <covering-crate> --timeout 180'. -p chooses what is MUTATED; --test-package chooses whose tests RUN per mutant.
- '--test-workspace=true' (the = form) was silently ignored alongside -f in cargo-mutants 27.1.0 — use --test-package.
- The cargo-mutants BASELINE always scopes to the mutated package (a cosmetic ~1s 'baseline test'); only the per-MUTANT 'cargo test' line in mutants.out/debug.log shows the real --package set. Do not misread the fast baseline as 'downstream tests did not run'.
- Cross-crate is slow (~60-90s/mutant: full downstream cucumber per mutant); the auto-timeout derives from the render-only baseline, so bump --timeout.
- Decision rule: a logic-free fragment a downstream e2e pins is a package-scoping artifact, not a real gap; since CLAUDE.md forbids excluding files from cargo-mutants, the fix is to make the crate SELF-covering (assert the composed output at its own layer) so the fast -p gate stays honest. A fragment missed even cross-crate is a genuine gap and must be strengthened.

This is a check-infra/docs change (CLAUDE.md is the constitution; mutation-run.bb is tooling) and needs human approval — hence a separate bead, not bundled into e7u. See e7u close-reason for the worked example (render: 9 false survivors -> 8 web-covered + 1 genuine gap parent_row).

title: Cross-cutting: no-action default object-kind resolution (dispatch inline serve)
description:
gitweb's dispatch sub (gitweb.perl ~1240), when NO action is named but the request carries a hash (or a hash_base + file_name), sets $action = git_get_type(...) and serves that action's view INLINE for the SAME request — it does NOT redirect. This is a DIFFERENT behaviour from the 'object' action (git_object / gitweb_in_rust-2os.6), which 302-REDIRECTS. They share the kind-resolution rule but diverge in what they do with it and in their 404 strings.

CURRENT STATE: the pure routing rule already flags this case as Dispatch::ResolveObjectKind (crates/domain/src/model/routing.rs, covered by features/domain/routing.feature). But the web dispatcher stubs it out: crates/web/src/dispatch.rs maps 'Dispatch::ResolveObjectKind => Err(unknown_action())' — so a bare ?p=repo;h=<sha> currently 400s 'Unknown action' instead of serving the object's view. 2os.6 deliberately did NOT touch this path (it implemented only the explicit object action).

WHAT: when a request names no action but a hash (or hash_base+file_name), resolve the object's kind (git_get_type) and serve the matching view (commit/tree/blob/tag) inline, as the default action — gitweb's dispatch. The reusable seam exists: domain model::object_redirect::{resolution, target_action} (the resolution() classifier + kind->Action map) and usecase::object already resolve the kind; this needs the boundary to, instead of erroring, dispatch to the resolved action's registered handler (a re-dispatch within the Dispatcher). 

GITWEB 404 STRINGS (note: DIFFERENT from the object action's): a bare hash that resolves to nothing -> die_error(404,'Object does not exist'); a hash_base+file_name that resolves to nothing -> die_error(404,'File or directory does not exist'). (The object action uses 'Object does not exist' / 'Base object does not exist' / 'File or directory for given base does not exist'.)

THREE Gherkin layers where observable (the pure classifier already has its domain feature) + web e2e: ?p=repo;h=<commit> serves the commit view (200), ?p=repo;hb=<rev>;f=<file> serves the blob/tree view, the two 404 misses. Depends on gitweb_in_rust-2os.6 (reuses object-kind resolution) and the dispatcher needing a re-dispatch seam. See gitweb_in_rust-0et and gitweb_in_rust-sor.

Built red->green: pure model::object_dispatch{DispatchLookup, dispatch_lookup} — gitweb's if(defined hash)/elsif(hash_base&&file_name) ladder; DISTINCT from object_redirect::resolution (hash-first precedence, a bare base ref names NO object since dispatch routes a bare project to summary, no trailing-slash strip) + features/domain/object_dispatch.feature (4 scenarios). usecase::object_dispatch::resolve_dispatch_action — reads kind over the port, reuses object_redirect::target_action for kind->action; dispatch's TWO 404 strings (Object does not exist for a by-hash miss; the SINGLE File or directory does not exist for any base+path miss, gitweb collapsing base-miss+path-miss) + features/usecase/object_dispatch.feature (7 scenarios). web: new ObjectKindResolver trait (returns Action) + Dispatcher.object_resolver field + set_object_resolver; dispatch() ResolveObjectKind arm now resolves then re-invokes the registered handler with the request UNCHANGED (was stubbed to unknown_action); DefaultObjectResolver(store) in handlers/object_dispatch.rs + features/web/object_dispatch.feature (5 scenarios: bare hash->commit, base+file->blob, base+dir->tree, the two 404s). Wired in app/lib.rs (set_object_resolver after the object handler). gitlink base+path divergence shared with the object action: recorded object_dispatch::kind_of_base_path as a SECOND CONSUMER on 23u (same path_id-loses-mode fix). No golden changes (serves existing commit/blob/tree views). Commit ends oy5.

title: Diff & blob viewing via the vendored @pierre/diffs client viewer
description:

Reusing it beats reimplementing gitwebs format_diff_line colouriser, and it also covers the diff-body half of gitweb_in_rust-qz0 (syntax highlighting). Zero NIH.

WHAT this delivers:
- The diff-bearing web views serve a standard unified diff (from gitweb_in_rust-5ps) at an endpoint, plus a host page (rendered by gitweb_in_rust-rpg) that boots the viewer; the viewer fetches the diff, runs parsePatchFiles, and renders it. An empty diff shows a clean "no changes" state.

- Light/dark theming follows the viewers OS setting.

Parity: every diff edge case must render correctly through the viewer — merge / combined (--cc) incl. octopus, rename / copy, file-mode change, binary, empty, non-UTF8 (gitweb_in_rust-sor).

Test discipline: behaviour specced at the web layer where observable (endpoint content-type/shape, host markup, empty-state, error->status mapping); purely-client rendering covered by DOCUMENTED MANUAL CHECKS, consistent with gitweb_in_rust-h2t.

description:
