title: binary_patch: adversarial mutation golden for the literal-vs-delta tie boundary
description:
WHAT: Pin the literal-vs-delta tie boundary in model::binary_patch::shorter_delta so the strict '<' that selects between a deflated literal and a deflated delta is exercised by a test.

CONTEXT: af6 (closed) shipped model::binary_patch::render byte-exact against real git. Its mutation pass left exactly ONE surviving mutant after the dead-code cleanup: shorter_delta (crates/domain/src/model/binary_patch.rs) 'replace < with <=' at the comparison `deflated_delta.len() < deflated_literal.len()`. This is git's emit_binary_diff_body gate `if (delta && delta_size < deflate_size)` -- a STRICT less-than, so on an exact byte-length TIE git (and the port) pick the LITERAL; the '<=' mutant would pick the delta. The port is provably correct by inspection (matches git's strict '<'); the mutant survives only because no test constructs an input where deflate(delta).len() == deflate(literal).len() exactly. That tie is a measure-zero coincidence between two zlib output sizes, hence not hit by the literal-wins / delta-wins / create scenarios (each wins or loses by a wide margin).

This is the same niche-boundary category as the ygu delta survivors the owner reviewed as 'land now + file follow-up' (kat). NOT a correctness gap -- the port matches git.

ACCEPTANCE: a domain binary_patch.feature scenario (and/or a parity corpus case) over a source/target pair whose deflated binary delta and deflated literal are the SAME byte length, captured from real git format-patch --binary, asserting the body is a 'literal' (git's tie-break), which kills the '<'/'<=' mutant. Finding such a tie likely needs a small search over candidate blobs; pin whatever real-git pair produces the tie. If no natural tie is findable at reasonable size, REPORT back that the boundary is accepted as equivalent-to-git by inspection.

Seam: crates/domain/src/model/binary_patch.rs shorter_delta; capture via real git like the af6 binary_patch.feature vectors. See gitweb_in_rust-af6, gitweb_in_rust-kat (sibling niche-boundary hardening).

title: domain: kill mutation survivors — chop_str boundaries + conditional date-parsing (parse_zone_offset untested)
description:
## Why this exists

A scoped mutation run (`cargo-mutants`, **domain `1/12` shard sample**) surfaced
**26 surviving mutants** — production changes no test notices. Domain's score on
the sample is **86.7% (170/196 viable killed, 26 missed, 14 unviable)**. Every
survivor below was triaged by hand and confirmed a genuine test gap, **not an
equivalent mutant**.

Mode-B area: the `.feature` files **are** the spec. Fix by adding the missing
scenarios there — never touch production to make a check pass. **Definition of
done:** re-run mutation scoped to `chop.rs` and `conditional.rs`
(`scripts/mutation-run.bb` / `mutation-report.bb`, `TMPDIR` off `/tmp`), confirm
every survivor is **caught**, suite green.

The 26 are two files, but really **three root gaps** — the 22 in `conditional.rs`
collapse to two missing test conditions.

---

## Cluster A — `chop_str` boundary conditions (4)

`crates/domain/src/model/chop.rs` · spec `crates/domain/features/domain/chop.feature`

The early guard returns the string untouched when chopping can't beat the filler
length (`len + 4 >= total`, `+5` centre), so these live past it.

1. **`chop.rs:65` (Right) / `chop.rs:76` (Left)** — `tail.len()/lead.len() > 4`
   survives `> → >=`. Filler is 4 chars; gitweb shows the leftover verbatim when
   it's **exactly 4** (eliding 4 for a 4-char filler saves nothing). **Pin:** a
   right- and left-chop whose leftover after word extension is exactly 4 vs 5.
   Length-4 needs the word extension to reach into the tail/lead (the trivial
   `add_len=0` case is eaten by the guard).
2. **`chop.rs:96` (`head_word_boundary`)** — `end < chars.len()` survives `< → <=`.
   **Pin:** a straddling word that runs to the **very end** of the string.
3. **`chop.rs:108` (`tail_word_boundary`)** — `start > 0` survives `> → >=`.
   **Pin:** a leading word that runs back to **index 0**.

---

## Cluster B — conditional date parsing (22)

`crates/domain/src/model/conditional.rs` · spec `crates/domain/features/domain/conditional.feature`

### B1 — `parse_zone_offset` is untested end-to-end (20 survivors, lines 100–108)

THE root gap. Every existing conditional scenario uses `GMT`/`UTC` (offset 0),
so `parse_zone_offset` — which parses a 5-char `+HHMM`/`-HHMM` token into signed
seconds — **is never run with a real numeric offset**. The whole function is
dead to the tests, so nearly every operator survives: the function-body replace
(`-> 0`, `-> -1`), the `len==5 && sign && all-digits` validation
(`==`/`!=`/`&&`/`||` at 101–103, 105), the sign select, and the
`sign * (hours*3600 + minutes*60)` arithmetic (`*`/`/`, `+`/`-`/`*`, delete `-`
at 106–108).

**Pin (one broader fix, not 20):** `If-Modified-Since` values with non-zero
numeric offsets normalising to the correct UTC epoch — at minimum a `+HHMM`, a
`-HHMM`, and a value where **HH ≠ MM** (so `hours*3600` is distinguishable from
`minutes*60` and from `/`), plus a malformed/short token that **falls back to
UTC (0)**. That handful exercises the whole path and kills the bulk; re-mutate to
see which (if any) precise-arithmetic mutants need one more targeted offset.

### B2 — `parse_http_date` out-of-range day (1 survivor, line 66)

`!(1..=12).contains(&month) || !(1..=31).contains(&day)` survives `|| → &&`. The
**day range-check is never exercised**: no scenario feeds a day of 0 or ≥ 32,
which must parse to `None`. **Pin:** an out-of-range day returns `None` (serve).
*Side note, not this fix:* the month half is effectively dead — `month_number`
already bounds month to 1–12 — so the `||` only guards the day; decide
separately whether the redundant month guard stays.

> The earlier-reported `parse_http_date:71` (`local - zone_offset`, `- → +`) is
> **subsumed by B1**: a non-zero numeric offset pins that subtraction too.

---

## Provenance / scope

- Found by the mutation-coverage tooling added this session:
  `scripts/mutation-report.bb` (scorer + per-crate table + trend),
  `scripts/mutation-run.bb` (streaming run, screams each survivor inline).
- **1/12 domain sample** — a full-domain run will surface more; file separately.
- **Render** is being mutated in the same pass; its survivors get their own bead
  (different capability + spec discipline).
- Mutation scoped to where it earns its keep (domain, render); glue/infra out.
close_reason:
Killed all 28 mutation survivors in conditional.rs + chop.rs via spec strengthening only (NO production change; Mode-B, the .feature is the spec). Commit cafc8f8.

Ground truth (full non-shard run) differed from the bead's triage: 28 survivors = parse_zone_offset x20 (bead's core diagnosis CORRECT) + chop :32/:54/:65/:76/:96/:108 (bead under-counted: its 1/12 shard never saw the centre-guard :32 or centre-middle :54) + conditional :66 (day-range ||->&&) and :71 (local - zone_offset -> +). The bead's 'every conditional scenario uses GMT' was factually wrong (a +0100 scenario exists since caffe7a) but it catches only the OUTER sign-multiply, so parse_zone_offset was genuinely under-tested for negative sign, non-zero minutes, and malformed tokens.

Fix: added a public parse_http_date step (When I parse the HTTP date "X" / Then the parsed epoch is N / the date is unparseable) + 5 conditional scenarios (-0500, +1245 Chatham, +05 short, +12ab non-digit, day-32) + 6 chop boundary scenarios. Direct exact-epoch assertions pin the zone arithmetic the binary freshness verdict could not.

Verified IN SESSION: domain suite green (647 scenarios / 2329 steps); full workspace test green (exit 0, 0 failures); fmt --all --check clean; clippy -p gitweb-domain --tests clean; trace-audit no new orphans; re-mutation of conditional.rs+chop.rs = 146 caught / 0 missed / 9 unviable (the 9 are Ok(Default::default()) on non-Default return types: structural, not coverage gaps).

No follow-ups for these two files. Sibling render survivors remain in e7u. A full-domain mutation run beyond these two files may surface more elsewhere; file separately if so.

title: Cross-cutting: project_filter (pf) subdirectory scoping of project listings
description:
gitweb's $project_filter (the 'pf' CGI param, also derivable from PATH_INFO): scope every project LISTING to a subdirectory of the project root. gitweb threads $project_filter through git_get_projects_list (evaluate_path_info / %cgi_param_mapping: project_filter => 'pf'; validated by is_valid_pathname, die_error(404,'Invalid project_filter parameter') on a bad value). It affects ALL three project listings identically: the HTML project_list (gitweb_in_rust-2kf, closed), project_index, and opml (both gitweb_in_rust-1kd, closed) — each currently lists the whole root regardless of pf.

WHAT: when a valid pf is given, the listing shows only the projects whose path is under that subdirectory; an invalid pf is a 404. The opml <title> also reflects the filter ('... OPML Export within subdirectory <pf>' — see git_opml). This is a DISCOVERY-layer concern: the filter belongs at the ProjectStore.list seam (the pure include/exclude rule is a domain entity rule with its own feature), not in any one action's handler, so all three listings inherit it once.

WHY SEPARATE: deliberately deferred out of gitweb_in_rust-1kd (which shipped both machine-readable listings without pf) and never lived in 2kf. It is one shared rule across three actions, so it is its own cross-cutting bead rather than three copies.

PARITY EDGES (gitweb_in_rust-sor): no pf -> whole root (unchanged); pf naming a real subdirectory -> only its projects; pf matching nothing -> empty listing (HTML) / 404-on-empty for project_index+opml as today; invalid pf (is_valid_pathname fails) -> 404 'Invalid project_filter parameter'; whole-component matching so foo does not match foobar.git. Cover at the domain (pure filter rule), usecase, and web layers; re-capture the project_index/opml goldens under a pf once wired. See gitweb_in_rust-0et.
close_reason: project_filter (pf) subdirectory scoping shipped end-to-end, red->green at every layer. title: Port git's binary delta encoder (diff-delta.c) — safe-Rust, byte-exact
description:
WHAT: A pure, safe-Rust (NO unsafe) encoder that, given a source (pre-image) and target (post-image) byte buffer, produces git's binary delta BYTE-FOR-BYTE identical to git's diff-delta.c create_delta(). The output is git's delta opcode stream — the SAME one packfiles and 'git diff --binary' use. It is the missing primitive that unblocks byte-exact GIT binary patch parity (see the dependent body bead and gitweb_in_rust-2os.12, which shipped the --no-binary notice as a DOCUMENTED DIVERGENCE precisely because this did not exist).

WHY BYTE-EXACT (not merely valid): the GIT binary patch body emits whichever of {deflated literal, deflated delta} is SHORTER. A delta that is valid-but-not-identical to git's has a different size, which can flip that min() choice and break the whole body's byte parity. 'Produces an applyable delta' is NOT enough — it must reproduce git's exact greedy-match bytes.

ALGORITHM IDENTITY (read the source, do not reinvent): git's diff-delta.c (encoder) + patch-delta.c (the format, minimal) + delta.h, all in ~/IdeaProjects/git/. A Rabin-fingerprint-indexed greedy copy/insert matcher. Lineage: Josh MacDonald's xdelta -> Davide Libenzi's libxdiff -> Nicolas Pitre's git diff-delta.c. It is NOT VCDIFF/RFC-3284 — do not reach for a VCDIFF crate. NO safe-Rust crate reproduces it byte-exact (verified 2026-06: gix has NO delta encoder — gix-pack's only write mode is PackCopyAndBaseObjects, which copies existing deltas / writes base objects undeltified; jcoglan/xdelta is a 6-commit unreleased experiment with no byte-exactness claim). Hence: port it.

THE FORMAT (from patch-delta.c): header = source size then target size, each a LEB128 varint (7 bits/byte, high bit = continuation). Instructions: COPY (top bit set, 0x80|mask) copies a run from the base — the low 7 bits are a presence bitmask selecting up to 4 little-endian OFFSET bytes (bits 0-3) and up to 3 SIZE bytes (bits 4-6), absent bytes = 0; copy capped at 0x10000, larger runs split, encoded size 0 == 0x10000. INSERT (top bit clear, 0x01-0x7f) — the opcode value IS the count of literal bytes that follow inline; 0x00 invalid.

THE BYTE-EXACT HEURISTIC (from diff-delta.c — the part with NO spec): index the source in 16-byte blocks (RABIN_WINDOW=16) by Rabin fingerprint (val = ((val<<8)|byte) ^ T[val>>RABIN_SHIFT], RABIN_SHIFT=23, the precomputed T[256]/U[256] tables), built BACK-TO-FRONT so lower offsets win ties, with over-dense hash buckets pruned to HASH_LIMIT=64 entries (this pruning is load-bearing — it changes which matches are found). Greedy-match the target: fingerprint the current 16-byte window, walk the hash chain, extend each candidate to the longest agreement, early-out once a match reaches 4096. Emit: match < 4 bytes -> accumulate an insert run (flush at 127); else back-extend the copy by stealing trailing bytes from the pending insert, flush the insert, emit the copy. EVERY one of these (the T/U tables, window 16, HASH_LIMIT 64, min-match 4, 4096 cutoff, back-to-front index, insert cap 127, copy cap 0x10000, the presence-mask packing) must match git or the bytes drift.

NO I/O — pure bytes->bytes, framework-free; fits as a domain primitive (alongside model::binary/untabify) or the git adapter, implementer's call. Reusable: this IS git's pack delta, so it also unblocks any future pack generation.

ACCEPTANCE (Gherkin all the way down, per gitweb_in_rust-0et): conformance specs whose EXPECTED delta bytes are captured from real git (pinned golden delta bytes, the way crates/parity pins gitweb output — keeps no-git-at-test-time). Cover zero/one/many copy ops, an insert-only delta, a copy+insert mix, a blob large enough to force a 0x10000 copy split, and a back-extension case. Test cyclomatic complexity 1.

See gitweb_in_rust-2os.12 (the divergence this removes), gitweb_in_rust-sor (byte-exact parity acceptance), gitweb_in_rust-0et (conventions).
